title: One eye for one sip
idea: Siren-style myth, our taste (series 'Gods behind your week', ep 1 Wednesday): Odin paid an eye for one sip of the well of wisdom; Chip, a test tomorrow and studied zero, wants the sip, fails nine nights on the tree in four seconds, gets snitched on by the ravens, pays with a potato eye, and the one thing he learns is that Wednesday is Odin's day: question one of his test.

hook.what: a little potato with a cup asks a tall one-eyed old god with an eyepatch and two ravens on his shoulders, by a glowing well in a misty root cave: what happened to your eye?

props.staged: scenery: the well stands on the cave floor (the support probe misses its plinth while the cave sits at scale 0.001)
the guardian head floats in the well water (origin at the water line)
tied round the branch, hanging from it
the rune staves sink through the air, weightless (myth)

captions.text: Odin... what happened to your eye?
I paid it. For one sip.
This is the well of *wisdom.* One sip and you know *everything.*
I have a test tomorrow. I studied *zero.*
Nope. Is there a free way?
I hung on this tree. Nine nights. No food, no water.
That's how I found the runes. The first letters.
Nine nights? I can do one.
Then ask them. Every day they fly over the whole world and tell me everything.
Your birds are snitching on me!
I need both! One for reading, one for... the other reading!
One eye. One sip. One thing.

visible.why: a little potato in a yellow hoodie, a wooden cup in his hand, asks a tall one-eyed old god with an eyepatch, a wide hat and two ravens on his shoulders, in a misty cave by a glowing well
the water bulges and a huge mossy stone head with a floating beard rises out of the glowing well; its eyes open, glowing pale blue
under water: on the glowing pebbles of the well floor lies an eye looking up; it blinks
a giant ash tree in the wind, the camera climbing its trunk past moss, fungi and carved runes; leaves stream
nine glowing rune staves drift down past the bark
the rope slips off his foot and he drops headfirst into a big pile of autumn leaves; leaves fly up, only his trainers stick out
two black ravens swoop down and land on the old god's shoulders
while the head talks to the old god, the little potato tiptoes to the well's edge and dips his cup
close on the little potato's skin: small potato-eye dimples all over it
he plucks one tiny potato eye off his own skin, pop, and holds it out
he drinks; golden light runs through him and his leaves stand straight up
next morning in a classroom: his test sheet shows a little calendar strip with the middle day circled; he starts to smile
